newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Business News - April 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Business News - April 14.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

In a deal which will make Ansett, Air New Zealand and Singapore Airlines significantly more competitive, the three airlines look set to form a far-reaching alliance to mirror the dominance of Qantas and British Airways on flights between Australia and Europe. Page 1.

In a deal keenly contested by Singapore and Malaysia, Australia has scored a significant success in the struggle to secure international business from its regional neighbours, with America's huge Digital Equipment Corp announcing it will establish a worldwide engineering facility in Sydney which is likely to generate A$100 million in annual exports within a few years. Page 1.

In a move which may signal to Prime Minister John Howard that the Native Title Act is feasible and does not need to be modified, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Commission chairman Ray Robinson has announced that RTZ-CRA's long-awaited A$1.1 billion Century Zinc project in Queensland will get approval from native title stakeholders at a signing ceremony in Mount Isa today. Page 5.

In a move aimed at strengthening Vodafone's position as a third force in Australian telecommunications alongside Telstra and Optus, it has unveiled plans to raise up to A$450 million through a public float of its Australian business, to coincide with the Sydney 2000 Olympics. Page 19.

Several broking houses have said that the proposed float of Colonial Mutual CGH.AX had been well received during the company's roadshow in Asia last week, despite the continuing correction of global equity markets. Australian investors, who have until May 2 to bid for stock, have also responded positively to the prospectus. Page 19.

In a strong result which reflects the dramatic emergence of the cotton industry from drought, the Namoi Cotton Co-operative, one of Australia's largest processors and marketers, has predicted a continued sharp improvement in its performance until 1999 after posting a A$6 million after-tax profit for the year to February. Page 19.
THE AUSTRALIAN

After the Dow Jones industrial average fell 148.36 points, or 2.27 per cent, to 6391.69 on Friday as a result of higher-than-expected US wholesale inflation figures, Australian investors are preparing for a multi-million slump in the domestic share market with the all ordinaries index expected to lose up to 40 points today. Page 17.

Following a move by Shell, BP, Mobil and Australian Petroleum (Caltex/Ampol) to virtually reject open access to storage terminals for independent operators, Australian Competition and Consumer Commission chairman Allan Fels said yesterday collusion betwen Australia's four major oil companies leading to the sharing of product continues to be a hurdle to increased price competition reform in the sector. Page 17.

Following a positive reaction in Asia to its polymer-based notes, the Reserve Bank - and its manufacturing subsidiary Note Printing Australia - is hoping to create a plastic single European currency after 1999 and is even planning to try and convince the conservative United States Congress to change the face of the US dollar. Page 17.

Speaking on the Nine Network's Business Sunday program yesterday, Federal Treasurer Peter Costello warned the business sector not to be "taken in" by the supporters of tax reform who were really promoting an anti-business agenda to boost Government spending. Page 19.

Allan Jones, the chief executive officer of the Namoi Cotton Co-operative - Australia's largest cotton processor - hopes to double last year's after-tax profit of A$6.1 million, with expectations of a profit of up to A$13 million. The strong forecast is a indication the company has recovered from drought, which, in 1995, saw the group using only 33 per cent of its capacity. Page 19.

In a move which stems from an extensive brand review undertaken last year, communications giant Telstra last night launched a multi-million dollar advertising campaign which ditches the national carrier's slogan of the past few years Advancing Australia in favour of a new slogan, Making Life Easier. The move comes ahead of the upcoming deregulation of the telecommunications industry and aims to unify its fragmented brand image. Page 19.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

The Australian sharemarket is expected to fall up to 40 points today after the Dow Jones index fell 148 points to 6391 on Friday - its lowest level for the year - amid expectations the United States Federal Reserve would raise interest rates to thwart inflation. Page 37.

In two notes to Insurance and Superannuation Commission staff last week, Commissioner George Pooley revealed he strongly supported recommendations in the Wallis report to create a mega-regulator for all financial institutions, saying the Commission stands to "gain greatly" from the move to shake-up prudential supervision. Page 37.

The battle-lines for Australia's A$700 million retail fruit-juice industry have been drawn as major players set the ground rules with a series of price wars. Golden Circle ignited the price war last week leaving market leaders National Foods and Berrivale considering a review of the number of brands each has on the market. Page 40.

Speaking after the release of the Australian Petroleum Production and Exploration Association's annual financial survey, chairman Nick Heath said a fresh approach is needed to encourage exploration in frontier deep water areas and called on the Federal Government to re-examine the oil and gas industry's tax regime. Page 37.

Speaking on the Nine Network's Business Sunday program yesterday, Business Council of Australia president Stan Wallis said he understood Federal Treasury was making a major reassessment of all tax concessions and deductions available to business but warned the Government not to make any short-term changes to business tax ahead of the next Budget. Page 37.

Despite an arrest warrant being issued last week, former high-flying businessman and now bankrupt Russell Goward, who has not been seen for the last four weeks, is yet to surface, with the New South Wales Police confirming yesterday that he had still not reported as required under his bail conditions. Goward was charged three years ago with giving false testimony to his bankruptcy trustee, Hugh Wily, of Armstrong Wily & Company. Page 39.
THE AGE

Australian shares are expected to plummet following Friday night's inflation driven share price drop in the US. Inflation fears are being driven by rising retail sales and higher then expected producer prices. The Dow Jones Industrial Index tumbled 148.6 points to close at 6391.69, the lowest drop for the year. Analysts are predicting that up to fifty points could be wiped off the Australian All Ordinaries in today's trading. Page B1.

The Federal Government is proposing that Australia Post become a provider of financial services and bank-style products to consumers in areas which have experienced closure of local banking facilities. The idea has been suggested by the Federal Treasurer Peter Costello who wishes non-bank financial institutions with extensive branch networks to offer more competition to the conventional banks. Page B1.

Telstra has launched a new A$120 million advertising and marketing campaign abandoning its long-standing Advance Australia image. The new campaign is aimed at facilitating Telstra's planned A$10 billion float later this year and providing a aggressive frnt against the increased telecommunications competition expected following further deregulation on 1 July. Page B1.

The Australian Manufacturing Workers Union said yesterday that Email workers have begun a state-wide stoppage at the Victorian operations. The strike began on Friday and the action is in response to a company offer of a pay rise of 2 to 3 per cent over the next two years. The workers are seeking a 15 per cent pay rise over the next two years. Page B1.

The Australian oil exploration and production industry managed to shed over A$700 million in operating costs last year, boosting profits by 10 per cent to A$1.67 billion despite lower oil prices. The figures were released in the annual survey of the indusry, issued by the Australian Petroleum Production and Exploration Association. Page B2.

Building materials group CSR is facing difficulties off-loading its A$1 billion timber division following rumours that bidders have only offered A$500 million, less then the division's book value. The market is now expecting CSR to announce that it will keep the timber division as it will only sell for a figure of A$900 million or more. Page B3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
